requirements.title: Build the repair queue from labels
requirements.rationale: What to repair, and in what order, follows from labels; a model deciding it would decide differently every time.

criteria.condition: the rules of a reconcile have been applied
criteria.action: queue every open issue labelled `af:defect` whose severity is in `--repair-on`, and every open `af:untested` issue when `--repair-on` holds `untested`, leaving out the issues labelled `af:repair-failed` and, unless `--repair-security` is given, the `security` defects
criteria.contract: the queue is ordered `security`, `data-loss`, `correctness`, `minor`, then `untested`, and within one of them oldest first by creation time; it holds at most `--repair-max` issues, 5 when the flag is absent; the issues beyond the cap are not repaired before the next reconcile

check.pseudocode: in internal/specrun/repair_test.go (new), a table over open issues and flags for the function that builds the queue: {minor (day 1), data-loss (day 3), correctness (day 2), untested (day 0), security (day 4), defaults -> [data-loss, correctness, minor, untested]; the same with --repair-security -> security first; two correctness of day 5 and day 2 -> day 2 first; --repair-on correctness,minor -> no data-loss and no untested; a defect labelled af:repair-failed -> left out; seven minor defects, default cap -> the five oldest; --repair-max 2 -> two; --repair-max 0 -> none; a closed defect -> left out; a deviation -> left out; a defect with no severity -> left out}

criteria.condition: a repair queue has been built and is not empty
criteria.action: run one repair step per issue, in queue order, before the next package
criteria.contract: the sessions after the reconcile are the repairs in order, then the next package; the rest of the queue is in the state file while it runs, and a restart goes on with it

setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
check.pseudocode: in internal/specrun/repair_test.go: with --reconcile-every 1, two open packages, and open defects minor and correctness: assert the session prompts are [01, reconcile, repair <correctness>, repair <minor>, 02, …]; stop the run after the first repair with --max and a state copy: assert the state file's queue holds the minor defect and a second run starts with its repair

criteria.action: take the kinds to repair, the cap per reconcile and whether security defects are repaired from them, each with its `SPECRUN_` variable as its default when set
criteria.contract: `--repair-on` is a comma-separated list of `security`, `data-loss`, `correctness`, `minor` and `untested`, the empty string meaning none; a value outside those, a negative `--repair-max` or one that is no integer is a usage error with exit code 2 naming the flag or the variable

requirements.title: Run a repair as a step of its own and check what it left
requirements.rationale: A session's last message is its own account; the forge and the repository are what happened.

criteria.condition: a repair step starts for an issue
criteria.action: start one session with the prompt `/af-impl --repair <issue number>`
criteria.contract: the session has the flags, the process group, the stream files and the stall rule of every session; its step name is `<n>-repair-<issue number>`

setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
check.pseudocode: in internal/specrun/repair_test.go: a queue holding issue 7: assert the fake claude's prompt is '/af-impl --repair 7' with the flags of a package session, and that <log dir>/000N-repair-7.jsonl exists

criteria.condition: a repair session ends, the base branch is checked out, the working tree is clean and the issue is closed
criteria.action: record the repair as done and go on
criteria.contract: the ledger line has kind `repair`, the issue number as its subject and outcome `already_fixed` when the merge commit at the tip of the base branch carries an `AF-Run:` trailer whose `repair.outcome` says so for this issue, else `fixed`

setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
check.pseudocode: in internal/specrun/repair_test.go, a table over a fake repair session that closes the issue and {merges with trailer repair.outcome 'fixed'; merges with 'already_fixed'; merges with no trailer; merges with a trailer naming another issue}: assert the ledger outcome is fixed, already_fixed, fixed, fixed, and the next step starts

criteria.condition: a repair session ends, the base branch is checked out, the working tree is clean and the issue is open and labelled `af:repair-failed`
criteria.action: record the repair as failed, and stop the loop when the issue carries a severity in `--stop-on`
criteria.contract: the ledger outcome is `failed`; with a severity in `--stop-on` the exit code is 1 and `result.stopped` names the issue with reason `repair failed`; otherwise the next step starts, and no later queue holds the issue while it keeps the label

check.pseudocode: in internal/specrun/repair_test.go, a table over a fake repair session that adds af:repair-failed to {a minor defect; a data-loss defect with the default --stop-on; a data-loss defect with --stop-on ''}: assert outcome 'failed' in each; assert exit code 1 and result.stopped only for the second; assert the next reconcile's queue leaves the issue out

criteria.condition: a repair session ends and the base branch is not checked out, the working tree is not clean, or the issue is open without `af:repair-failed`
criteria.contract: exit code 1; `result.stopped.reason` names what the session left (`not on the base branch`, `working tree not clean`, `issue neither closed nor marked failed`); the ledger outcome is `stopped`; no further session starts

criteria.condition: `specrun` is started and its state records a repair step as running
criteria.action: count the repair as done when its issue is closed, and run it again otherwise
criteria.contract: a closed issue gets a ledger line with outcome `fixed` and no session; an open one gets a session with the same prompt

requirements.title: Repair a serious defect instead of stopping
requirements.rationale: Stopping is right when nobody is there to decide; with permission to repair, the loop can clear the defect and go on.

criteria.condition: `--repair` is given and a package has landed with open defects of a severity in `--stop-on`
criteria.action: repair each of them, most severe first then oldest first, before the next package, and make the stop check again afterwards
criteria.contract: the sessions after the package are one repair per such defect, with no cap; when every one is closed the next package starts; a defect that is still open after its repair stops the loop as the stop rule does

setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
check.pseudocode: in internal/specrun/repair_test.go, a table with --repair and --repair-security over what the fake session of 01 leaves and what the repairs do: {data-loss and security, both fixed -> prompts [01, repair security, repair data-loss, 02]; data-loss, repair marks it failed -> exit code 1 after one repair; a correctness defect alone -> no repair, 02 starts}

criteria.condition: `--repair` is given without `--repair-security` and a package has landed with an open `security` defect
criteria.action: stop the loop without repairing it
criteria.contract: exit code 1 with the stop rule's `result.stopped`; no repair session starts for the security defect

requirements.title: Show the repair queue in a dry run
requirements.rationale: A person deciding whether to allow repairs wants to see what would be repaired.

criteria.condition: `--dry-run` is given and a forge client can be made
criteria.action: report the repair queue as the labels now stand
criteria.contract: `result.repair_queue` lists each issue with its number, title, URL and severity or `untested`, in queue order and capped by `--repair-max`; it is `[]` when the queue is empty; no session starts and the forge records no write

setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
check.pseudocode: in internal/specrun/repair_test.go: with open defects minor and correctness and an untested item: run --dry-run --repair-max 2; assert result.repair_queue names the correctness and the minor defect in that order; assert no session and no forge write

execution_paths.title: specrun repairs a defect and an untested item after a reconcile

steps.action: runs `specrun --reconcile-every 1` with an open correctness defect and an open untested item on the forge
lands the next package, runs the reconcile and builds the repair queue from the labels: the defect, then the untested item
starts a repair session for the defect
branches, writes the regression test, sees it fail, fixes the code, passes the full gate that speca runs, merges and closes the issue
runs the full gate for the repair and answers `pass`
checks the base branch and the issue, records `fixed`, and starts the repair of the untested item
writes the missing test, sees it pass on the unchanged code, commits it, merges and closes the issue with an `already_fixed` trailer
records `already_fixed` and goes on to the next package
